_about: Hindcast default parameter space, tier S (ShadowLoop proposal section 4, DESIGN.md section 5.4).
One entry per VDF key "<array> <item>": type float/int (low, high, step: the searched step grid), bool, or
choice (explicit values). "phone" is the current value in ns_settings.json (the centre of the one-at-a-time
screen and the sentinel); regenerate with `python -m hindcast.space --write-defaults` after a preferences import.
Constraints are ordering chains the sampler keeps by construction. Locked keys (DESIGN.md section 3: safety
section, profile sens/carb_ratio/current_basal/dia, every new_parameter key) stay locked unless a study unlocks them explicitly.
This file says what a replay may vary; it recommends nothing. Nothing in Hindcast changes the phone.
Tier S: the safety caps max_iob and max_basal (locked by default: a study needs --unlock KEY --unlock-reason TEXT, stored in study.json). maxSMBBasalMinutes / maxUAMSMBBasalMinutes are in tier B.
A cap study only reports how often the cap binds and how the decisions move when it does; it cannot say what the extra or missing insulin would have done. Weak evidence; for review by hand.
_evidence: weak: decision-level replay, no glucose response

profile max_iob._note: Weak evidence: decision-level replay, no glucose response - the replay keeps the glucose and insulin history the phone's own settings produced, so it says how the decisions would have moved, never what glucose would have done. Safety cap (U): a cap study only reports how often and in which loops the cap binds (insulinReq / SMB limited by max_iob, iobTH = iob_threshold_percent of it) and how much more or less the loop would have asked; it cannot show what the extra or missing insulin would have done.

profile max_basal._note: Weak evidence: decision-level replay, no glucose response - the replay keeps the glucose and insulin history the phone's own settings produced, so it says how the decisions would have moved, never what glucose would have done. Safety cap (U/h) on every temp basal: a cap study only reports how often the TBR cap binds. ns_profile derives the profile value as min(max(preference, max_daily_basal), floor(current_basal_safety_multiplier * basal), floor(max_daily_safety_multiplier * max_daily_basal)); a VDF row replaces that derived value with the raw number (also the sentinel row), so it can differ from base where the derivation does not return the preference.
